text:
oncall-marc: 14:02 UTC - noticed increased 5xxs from asia-east-1 GPUs, traffic spiking to eu fallback.
quinn: rolling alerts show GPU host churn, autoscaler couldn't place pods due to quota, routing started shifting to asia-edge-2 which has smaller capacity :grimacing:
maria: can we trigger DNS failover to asia-standby now? current A/AAAA RRset has geo weights, but some resolvers are still honoring old entries.
irfan: before we touch DNS, check authoritative TTLs. I see TTL=300 on the zone. that's too long for an active failover.
sre-jen: agree — let's set a short TTL, but remember propagation to ISPs will be slower if caches ignore shorter TTLs. Recommend set TTL=60 then update RRset.
oncall-marc: ok, changing TTL to 60 on cloud-dns. Doing in 2m. Heads-up: we'll also rotate RRset to point to standby pool.
quinn: noted. Watch for resolver caching; end-to-end we'll likely see partial shift for ~5-15min depending on ISPs.
maria: command I'm running:
```
# update TTL
gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=redwood-infra
gcloud dns record-sets transaction remove --name "infer.redwood.ai." --type A --ttl 300 --zone=redwood-infra --rrdatas "34.78.90.12"
gcloud dns record-sets transaction add --name "infer.redwood.ai." --type A --ttl 60 --zone=redwood-infra --rrdatas "34.78.90.12"
gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=redwood-infra
```
irfan: after TTL change, update weights. I'm going to reduce primary weight to 0 and add standby IPs. I'll keep a small % to primary for slow drain.
sre-jen: remember to adjust healthcheck TTL too (route-based). we should keep fast healthcheck probes to avoid flipping back-and-forth.
oncall-marc: done with TTL change, timestamp 1842004360. Also created a rollback txn.
deploy-bot: deploy status: DNS zone update accepted (tx id: tx-7821) — propagation to authoritative nameservers in progress.
quinn: starting RR rotation now. I'm patching the RRset to replace primary IPs with standby pool (asia-standby: 13.32.45.67, 13.32.45.68).
maria: patch applied 1842004410. Verified authoritative answers from ns1/ns2 show new RRset with TTL=60.
irfan: running dig from multiple vantage points:
```
dig +tcp @ns1.infra.redwood.net infer.redwood.ai A +short
# returns 13.32.45.67
dig @8.8.8.8 infer.redwood.ai A +short
# still returns 34.78.90.12 (cached)
```
oncall-marc: expected. We'll see mixed responses until resolver caches expire or respect new TTL. Start routing fallback in the loadbalancer too so sessions are sticky.
quinn: note: some corporate resolvers ignore low TTL (caching at 300). We should plan a gradual reweighting and not hard-cut primary to 0 until backend pressure is confirmed lower.
sre-jen: also saw anomalous negative caching from an ISP — NXDOMAIN responses cached. I've pumped a synthetic query to clear local caches: `dig +bufsize=4096 @resolver infer.redwood.ai` might help.
maria: cost note — bursting to standby increases egress/cycle costs ~2x due to cross-region routing. Heads-up to finance but reliability first.
irfan: cluster update: autoscaler quota request for asia-east-1 in-flight. If quota not approved in 30m we'll be on standby longer. Consider warm pools in us-west as alternate.
oncall-marc: monitoring: added dashboard for RRset composition + resolver discrepancy count. Initial skew: 40% still seeing old IPs.
quinn: can we also reduce authoritative TTL further to 30? Might be risky. Let's hold at 60 for 30 minutes then consider lowering.
sre-jen: agree. Also add a public notice to status.redwood.ai to explain degraded performance in Asia and DNS failover in progress — reduces pager noise.
maria: status update posted.
deploy-bot: alert: 1842004525 — traffic shift completed to standby pool per LB metrics; backend error rates decreasing.
oncall-marc: excellent. Continue monitoring for residual 5xxs. If load increases on standby beyond safe thresholds we'll scale up reserved nodes, but that's an ops ticket.
quinn: after 20m we should roll TTL back to 300 to reduce DNS churn. Add a follow-up to revert TTL once normal.
irfan: capturing all steps for post-incident doc: TTL change, RR rotation, LB fallback, synthetic queries, scaling/quotas, cost tradeoffs, rollback plan.
sre-jen: postmortem owners: irfan + maria. oncall-marc will run incident summary.
oncall-marc: wrapping up. Final note: remember that some ISPs will still hold prior RRsets for 24-48h despite low TTLs due to broken resolvers. We'll record which ASN/vendors showed the slowest convergence.
quinn: thumbs up :thumbsup:
